name: Replika – The AI Companion
y2026_hot: Goes live amid ongoing AI‑embodied companionship boom and regional privacy regulation scrutiny, with 40M+ users and ~25% paying subscribers.
origin: Born from a journalist’s grieving friend’s chat logs; the founder digitised their exchange to build a conversational AI friend.

milestones.outcome: Idea born from a deceased friend’s chat logs
milestones.detail: Founder Eugenia Kuyda digitised her late friend’s messages to create the first prototype.
Replika launched as a free mobile app on iOS and Android in November 2017, reaching 2M users by early 2018.
The Italian Authority banned Replika’s data usage; the company removed erotic chat features and later restored them for pre‑2023 users.
Replika reported surpassing 30M global users after expanding its premium freemium model.
Dmytro Klochko became CEO, steering the company toward deeper AI‑driven therapy niche and further scale.

turning_points: Italian ban forcing feature removal and privacy compliance overhaul
failures: Regulatory ban in Italy requiring removal of erotic features; led to user trust erosion
lessons: AI services must align with region‑specific privacy law; compliance is essential for trust
Balancing free access with paid premium features can sustain growth
